design_rationale: Participants were randomly allocated 1:1 to either the experimental or control group using a computer-generated sequence via www.randomization.com.

domain_judgments.rationale: The allocation sequence was generated using an online tool, concealed in opaque envelopes managed by an independent secretariat, and baseline characteristics were well balanced between groups.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: The randomization of group allocation (allocation ratio = 1:1 – control group: experimental group) followed the online tool www. randomization.com. The code and group allocation of each participant was packed into concealed opaque envelopes. The envelopes were stored at the urogynecology secretariat. Physiotherapists treating participants were informed about group allocation of their participant by the independent urogynecology secretariat.

domain_judgments.rationale: Participants and investigators were blinded to assignment, interventions adhered to standardized protocols with high adherence across both groups, and an intention-to-treat approach was applied.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: This investigation was designed as a triple-blind (participants, investigators, statistician) prospective randomized controlled trial with two PT intervention groups. This means that participants, investigators and the statistician had no knowledge of the group assignment of the participants.

domain_judgments.rationale: A small number of randomized participants dropped out before baseline or during follow-up, and missing values were handled using last observation carried forward (LOCF), which can potentially bias longitudinal estimates.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: Subsequently, baseline assessment of 45 (EXP) and 47 (CON) participants was completed, as 4 participants were lost after randomization (EXP: due to personal reasons n = 1, medical problems n = 2; CON: not available n = 1). Furthermore, 8 participants had incomplete primary outcome data (EXP: lost to follow-up post measurement (n = 1, discontinued intervention n = 3; CON: discontinued intervention n = 4). Based on the intention-to-treat approach and the applied last observation carried forward method, missing data were replaced by the last valid data of the respective participant

domain_judgments.rationale: The primary outcome is a validated patient-reported questionnaire, administered identically across groups with participants and outcome assessors blinded to group allocation.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: This investigation was designed as a triple-blind (participants, investigators, statistician) prospective randomized controlled trial with two PT intervention groups. This means that participants, investigators and the statistician had no knowledge of the group assignment of the participants. ... Primary outcome was the International Consultation on Incontinence Modular Questionnaire Urinary Incontinence short form (ICIQ-UIsf).

domain_judgments.rationale: The study had an a priori protocol published and registered on ClinicalTrials.gov, and the outcomes were reported according to pre-specified analysis plans without evidence of selective reporting.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: The study protocol was approved by the Ethics Committee of the Canton of Bern, Switzerland (reference number 249/14), registered at (www.clinicaltrials. gov; study identifier: NCT02318251), and published including the detailed intervention PFMT description as “Additional file” [16].

overall_summary: The trial was generally well-conducted and triple-blinded with proper randomization and pre-registration; however, there are some concerns regarding missing outcome data due to participant dropouts and the use of last observation carried forward (LOCF) for imputation.

design_rationale: Participants were randomly allocated using computer-generated random block sequences via an independent web-based randomisation service.

domain_judgments.rationale: The allocation sequence was generated via a computer-based clinical trials unit web service with stratified block randomization, ensuring allocation concealment and producing balanced baseline groups.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: Randomisation was by computer allocation using the web-based randomisation service of the Norwich Clinical Trials Unit. To ensure the treatment groups were similar a stratified randomisation with 3 strata (i.e., low SSI; high SSI/low BMI; high SSI/ high BMI) was used. In each stratum, balanced blocks of random length (4, 6 or 8) were fitted to assign an equal number of SPC + MP and SPC participants.

domain_judgments.rationale: Participants and care providers could not be blinded to the behavioral exercise intervention, and the primary analysis was a complete-case per-protocol analysis excluding participants who failed to attend treatments rather than a full intention-to-treat analysis.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: From the 36 women allocated to the intervention (SPC + MP) group and the 37 women allocated to the control (SPC group), 14 and 10 women respectively were removed from the complete case analysis for the following reasons: failed to attend the scheduled treatments (10 SPC + MP; 7 SPC), medical reasons (1 SPC + MP; 1 SPC), lost to follow-up (3 SPC + MP; 2 SPC).

domain_judgments.rationale: Approximately 33% of randomized participants (24 of 73; 39% in intervention vs 27% in control) were excluded from the analysis with no imputation or evidence that missingness was independent of true outcome.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: From the 36 women allocated to the intervention (SPC + MP) group and the 37 women allocated to the control (SPC group), 14 and 10 women respectively were removed from the complete case analysis for the following reasons: failed to attend the scheduled treatments (10 SPC + MP; 7 SPC), medical reasons (1 SPC + MP; 1 SPC), lost to follow-up (3 SPC + MP; 2 SPC). This left a total of 49 participants...

domain_judgments.rationale: The primary outcomes were self-reported subjective questionnaires assessed in unblinded participants aware of their allocation status.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: Due to the nature of the intervention blinding of participants, physiotherapists and researchers was not feasible... Main outcome measures were self-reported UI, quality of life and self-esteem at baseline (T1), completion of treatment (T2), and 5 months after randomisation (T3).

domain_judgments.rationale: The trial was registered retrospectively, and multiple subscale outcomes and subgroup/strata comparisons were analyzed and highlighted after main pre-post comparisons were non-significant, without an explicit pre-specified statistical analysis plan.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: Trial registration: ISRCTN74075972 Registered 12/12/12 (Retrospectively registered)... Post-intervention participants in the SPC + MP group with low SSI showed significant increases in self-esteem (standardized effect size d = 0.79, p = 0.032)...

overall_summary: The study has high overall risk of bias driven primarily by substantial and unbalanced missing outcome data (approximately 33% overall attrition excluded from complete-case analysis), along with some concerns regarding lack of participant blinding on self-reported outcomes, non-ITT analysis, and potential selective reporting across multiple subgroup/scale analyses.

design_rationale: The authors explicitly state that participants were randomly assigned to one of two arms using a table of random numbers prepared by a biostatistician with a block size of 4 and stratification by age and place of residence.

domain_judgments.rationale: The allocation sequence was generated using a table of random numbers with blocking and stratification, and allocation was concealed by a central research coordinator blinded to participant status.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: Participants were randomized to one of two arms, Paula or PFMT instruction, using a table of random numbers prepared by a biostatistician, with a block size of 4. The randomization was stratified by age (20–50 and 51–65) and place of residence (three towns). The nurses (including the PI) who performed the pad test before and after the intervention were blinded to the intervention arm. The randomization list was kept by the research coordinator, and the code was not broken until the last participant completed her postintervention pad test.

domain_judgments.rationale: Due to the behavioral exercise nature of the interventions, participants were aware of their assignment, and the primary analysis excluded participants who dropped out rather than adhering to a full intention-to-treat framework.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: A total of 176 of 240 (73.3%) participants were evaluable for assessment of the primary end point after the intervention, 92 of 117 (78.6%) in the Paula group and 84 of 123 (68.3%) in the PFMT group... We performed a best case–worst case scenario in order to approximate an intention-to-treat analysis.

domain_judgments.rationale: Substantial missing outcome data (26.6% overall, with higher attrition in PFMT [31.7%] than Paula [21.4%]) occurred, and sensitivity analyses (best/worst case) demonstrated that missingness could impact equivalence versus non-inferiority conclusions.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: The study was limited by a dropout rate of 26.6%... A total of 176 of 240 (73.3%) participants were evaluable for assessment of the primary end point after the intervention, 92 of 117 (78.6%) in the Paula group and 84 of 123 (68.3%) in the PFMT group, the others having dropped out after beginning the intervention or having failed to appear for the final Pad test evaluation (p = 0.07).

domain_judgments.rationale: The primary outcome (1-hour clinical pad test) is an objective weight measurement, and the nurses administering and evaluating the test were masked to treatment assignment.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: The nurses (including the PI) who performed the pad test before and after the intervention were blinded to the intervention arm.

domain_judgments.rationale: No clinical trial registration number or published pre-specified statistical analysis protocol is reported, creating some concerns regarding selective outcome reporting.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: The primary outcome was change in the quantity of urinary leakage, measured by the 1-hour clinical pad test. Secondary outcomes included a subjective assessment of urinary symptoms... We also administered a QOL questionnaire...

overall_summary: The overall risk of bias is high due to substantial and differentially distributed missing outcome data (>26% dropout), which had a demonstrable potential to affect trial equivalence/superiority conclusions.

design_rationale: Participants were randomly assigned to the experimental and control groups using EpiData version 3.1 software.

domain_judgments.rationale: Although computer randomization was used, allocation concealment is not reported, and there was a baseline imbalance in climacteric status (82% vs 44%, P = 0.02).
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: Forty women were randomly assigned to the experimental and control groups by the EpiData version 3.1® program using the contact list as reference for the allocation drawing.

domain_judgments.rationale: Participants could not be blinded to exercise physical therapy interventions, and the analysis excluded participants lost to follow-up (complete-case analysis rather than true intention-to-treat).
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: Due to lost to follow-up, 33 ofthe 40 women in the intervention groups were considered for statistical analysis, 17 in the experimental group and 16 in the control group (Fig. 1).

domain_judgments.rationale: Attrition was relatively low and balanced between groups (3/20 [15%] experimental vs. 4/20 [20%] control), making substantial bias from missing data unlikely.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: Due to lost to follow-up, 33 ofthe 40 women in the intervention groups were considered for statistical analysis, 17 in the experimental group and 16 in the control group (Fig. 1).

domain_judgments.rationale: Outcome assessors were blinded to group allocation, and validated questionnaires and voiding diaries were used consistently across groups.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: All evaluations were performed by an uninformed physiotherapist regarding the allocation of women in the intervention groups.

domain_judgments.rationale: The trial was pre-registered in the Brazilian Registry of Clinical Trials database (RBR-2HB4P8), and all pre-specified outcomes are reported with expected analyses.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: Study organized according to Resolution 466/12, approved by the Research Ethics Committee of the Federal University of Juiz de Fora (opinion 190.572) and registered in the Brazilian Registry of Clinical Trials database (RBR-2HB4P8).

overall_summary: The study has some concerns overall driven by unclear allocation concealment with a baseline imbalance in climacteric status (Domain 1), as well as lack of participant blinding with complete-case analysis (Domain 2).

design_rationale: The study states that participants were randomly grouped into group A and group B to receive the interventions.

domain_judgments.rationale: The paper states participants were randomly grouped but does not describe the random sequence generation method or allocation concealment.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: The participants were randomly grouped into group A and B . Group A includes 15 females and underwent kegels training and group B with 15 females and received kegels combined with Pallof press exercise.

domain_judgments.rationale: Participants could not be blinded to exercise conditions, and there is no information on intervention adherence or deviation monitoring, though an appropriate per-protocol/complete case analysis appears to include all 30 participants.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: Group A received exercise of 3 sets per day daily for 8 weeks. Group B was given kegels and Pallof press exercise daily for a period of 8 weeks.

domain_judgments.rationale: Outcome data appear to be available for all 30 randomized participants (15 per group) with no reported dropouts.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: 30 female subjects were selected based on the inclusion criteria for the experiment... Group A includes 15 females and underwent kegels training and group B with 15 females

domain_judgments.rationale: The outcomes (RUIS and IIQ-7) are patient-reported questionnaires completed by participants who were aware of their assigned intervention group.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: RUIS and IIQ 7 were taken on the first day and after the 8th week.

domain_judgments.rationale: There is no evidence of a prospective trial registration or pre-specified analysis plan, and the reported statistical comparisons are inconsistent and problematic (e.g., claiming group differences while reporting identical within-group Wilcoxon test statistics across tables).
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: In comparison of post test scores of outcome measures evidenced that the reduction in the urinary incontinence frequency and improvement in quality of life scores were significantly more among the women s treated with combined kegels and pallof press exercise than with women s treated with kegels alone .

overall_summary: The overall risk of bias is high due to substantial concerns regarding the selection of reported results, including inconsistent and flawed reporting of statistical analyses without pre-registration, alongside lack of details on sequence generation and allocation concealment.

design_rationale: Participants were randomly allocated to either the Paula method or pelvic floor muscle training using a random number table with block randomization stratified by age.

domain_judgments.rationale: The sequence was generated using a random number table with block randomization, but there is no information detailing how allocation concealment was achieved before assignment.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: Randomization was performed according to a random number table in blocks of four. The randomization was stratified by age only into two groups: 25–50 years and 51–65 years. After randomization the participants were informed about treatment allocation by the principal investigator.

domain_judgments.rationale: Participants and exercise instructors could not be blinded to the behavioral exercise interventions, and a per-protocol complete-case analysis was performed excluding 4 randomized participants (2 per group) rather than an intention-to-treat analysis.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: Of these, two women stopped exercising after 1 week (one from each group) and two randomized women did not start exercising (one from each group). Those four women were not evaluable for outcome assessments and therefore were not included in the study results (Fig. 1). In total, 30 women in the Paula group and 29 women in the pelvic floor training group received the intended treatment, completed the study protocol, and were analyzed for the primary and secondary outcomes.

domain_judgments.rationale: Missing outcome data were minimal (4 out of 63 participants, ~6.3%), balanced equally across the two arms (2 in each group), and unlikely to bias results substantially.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: Thus, 63 women were included in the study and were randomized. Of these, two women stopped exercising after 1 week (one from each group) and two randomized women did not start exercising (one from each group). Those four women were not evaluable for outcome assessments and therefore were not included in the study results (Fig. 1).

domain_judgments.rationale: The primary outcome (pad test) was administered and measured by unblinded staff (the principal investigator who informed participants of allocation, or registered nurses with unstated blinding status), and subjective quality of life outcomes were self-reported by unblinded participants.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: The primary outcome was a change in urinary leakage measured by a 1-h pad test [17], performed by the principal investigator (M. Liebergall-Wischnitzer) or by trained registered nurses... The study gynecologists were blinded to allocation.

domain_judgments.rationale: No pre-registered trial protocol is cited, and the trial evaluated multiple outcomes and subscales with statistical testing focused almost entirely on within-group differences rather than randomized between-group comparisons.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: This pilot study was designed to measure within-group diferences and not between-group efects.

overall_summary: The study has some concerns regarding risk of bias due to lack of reported allocation concealment, unblinded participants and outcome assessors for several key endpoints (including pad test administration and patient-reported outcomes), complete-case per-protocol analysis excluding four randomized participants, and absence of a pre-registered statistical analysis plan with analysis limited primarily to within-group comparisons.

design_rationale: The study explicitly describes random allocation using computer-generated block randomization with allocation managed by an independent researcher.

domain_judgments.rationale: Random sequence generation and allocation concealment were appropriately performed, and baseline characteristics appeared balanced between groups.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: They were allocated according to computer-generated block randomization (http://www.randomization.com). A different researcher was in charge of the allocation; therefore, the investigator and the blind evaluator did not have access to the randomization list generated by the computer.

domain_judgments.rationale: Patients and treating physical therapists could not be blinded given the nature of the exercise interventions, and a complete-case analysis was conducted rather than a true intention-to-treat analysis.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: In the study protocol, none of the patients changed their allocated group. However, the 4 patients who interrupted the protocol were not evaluated at the end of the study because of difficulty in contacting. ... Finally, the intention-to-treat analysis was not performed.

domain_judgments.rationale: Loss to follow-up was low (4/47, ~8.5%) and balanced across the two groups (2 dropped out per group).
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: A total of 47 women with SUI were randomly assigned to either the PF group or the PFH group. Four women did not complete the study because of personal issues, resulting in 21 participants in the PF group and 22 in the PFH group (Fig 3).

domain_judgments.rationale: Physical evaluations and questionnaire assessments were performed by an assessor blinded to treatment allocation, and patient-reported diaries followed standardized procedures across groups.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: The assessor, who was blind to the group allocation, was a physiotherapist with 10 years’ experience in physiotherapy for women’s health, with a focus on pelvic floor dysfunctions. The primary outcome measure was the frequency of urine leakage. Secondary outcomes were strength and function of the pelvic floor and QoL.

domain_judgments.rationale: The trial was prospectively registered, and the reported outcomes match the pre-specified primary and secondary outcomes.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: Our trial was prospectively registered at ClinicalTrials.gov (identification number NCT01948713) and followed the CONSORT guidelines. There was no deviation from the protocol.

overall_summary: The study is generally well-conducted with computer randomization, allocation concealment, and assessor blinding, but raises some concerns regarding deviations from intended interventions due to lack of participant blinding and failure to conduct an intention-to-treat analysis.
